root.name: Scotch Game: Meitner Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Bc5 5. Be3 Qf6 6. c3 Nge7 7. Nc2

overview: In the Scotch Classical with 4...Bc5 5.Be3 Qf6 6.c3 Nge7 White has strengthened d4 with c3 and plays 7.Nc2, preparing Bd3 and O-O. Black has a developed position with the queen out early, and both sides aim for a solid centre. The play is positional and open.

white_ideas.idea: Support the centre with c3 and Nc2
Take the bishop pair if the bishop retreats

typical_structures.structure: Scotch pawn centre with c3 and e4

structure.notes: Open lines after the d4 exchange.

approach.notes: Scotch is a normal main line.

character.reason: Neither side is forced into risks and the position is not hard to break.

soundness.reason: Both sides play natural, accepted moves.

structure.reason: The Scotch centre is open after the exchange on d4.

approach.reason: A normal branch of the Scotch.

level.reason: Plans are clear and not heavy on theory.

plans.reason: White's c3/e4 centre is the main asset.
